1.why: All 11 screenshots show static pages with plain layout and no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs anywhere.

2.why: Primary buttons are dark navy against a light background, headings are large, and messages are color-coded (green success text, bordered 'Stay safe' box), making key elements visually prominent.

3.why: Each page presents one labeled task with a single input and button under persistent 'Request reset / Enter code / Sign in' tabs, though after requesting a code the user must infer on her own to open the 'Enter code' tab.

4.why: Password rules and the 15-minute code-expiry rule are printed on the page rather than requiring memorization, but the flow spans about seven steps across three tabs with two distinct codes to handle.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill indicator, or password-manager affordance appears on any of the forms shown.

6.why: Nothing is pre-filled from saved data and there are no recognition aids such as masked account hints; Helena must recall her registered contact and new password from memory.

7.why: Screens use short, plain sentences ('Enter the one-time security code'), though a few phrases are abstract, e.g., 'For privacy, the result is the same whether or not an account is found' and 'If eligible'.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the 11 steps, so there is no observed error text that describes a problem and how to fix it.

9.why: Fields give format hints ('Use an email-style contact value', password composition rules) but no concrete worked example; only the training-only mock codes displayed in the Logs panel act as literal fill-in values.

10.why: Only password plus one-time code sign-in is offered and each is clearly labeled ('Sign in securely', 'Verify security code'); no face login exists and there are no competing methods to confuse.

11.why: Every screen contains a single primary action with at most three persistent navigation tabs, so the number of simultaneous choices is minimal.

12.why: Bold green confirmations state outcomes ('Security check complete. You may review the privacy conditions.', 'Updated privacy conditions have been accepted.'), though saving the password and verifying the reset code advance silently via page change.

13.why: Each new step carries a short inline tip (email-format hint, code expiry note, password rules, 'the mock code is shown in the Logs panel'), but no dedicated help resource is present.

14.why: No error or retry state is shown in the screenshots and requests are explicitly rate-limited ('Requests are limited for your protection'), so ease of trying again cannot be confirmed.

15.why: The header, tabs, card layout, color scheme, button styling, and Logs panel are identical across all 11 steps, giving a fully consistent design.
